High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Akhilendra Singh, learned Government Advocate for   respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No.32840/2024, which is tenth application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant Kedar.
His first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 04.03.2014.

The appellant stands convicted for the offence under Sections 3/4, 5 J(II)(L)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 and Section 376(2)(Jha) of IPC and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with fine of Rs.25,000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.25,000/- and life imprisonment with fine of Rs.50,000/- respectively with default stipulations, vide judgment dated 04.09.2013 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge, Balaghat (M.P.) in S.T. No.110/2013.
The prosecution story found to be proved is that the appellant committed forceful sexual intercourse upon the minor prosecutrix repeatedly due to which she became pregnant.
On the basis of aforesaid guilt, the appellant has been convicted and sentenced, as mentioned above.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
FIR has been lodged with 2 CRA-2617-2013 a delay of 5-6 months.
FSL and DNA report is negative.
No injury has been found on the private part of the prosecutrix.
It is submitted that looking to the age of the prosecutrix, she is found to be 14 years and two years more or less is possible as per ossification report.
Learned counsel further contended that the appellant remained under custody almost about 12 years.
The appeal is of the year 2013 and there is no likelihood of early hearing of this appeal, therefore, jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
Per contra, learned Government Advocate has vehemently opposed the application for suspension of sentence and submitted that looking to the gravity of offence, the application may be rejected.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard the arguments of the parties and the fact that no internal injury has been found on the body of the prosecutrix, FSL and DNA report is negative and the appellant remained under custody almost about 12 years, we deem it appropriate to suspend the jail sentence of appellant and to release him on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A. No. 32840/2024 is allowed.

It is directed that substantive jail sentence of appellant Kedar shall remain suspended subject to his depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on 24.06.2025 and on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Court concerned in this behalf.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
